svg.title: STC-09 · Evoke the genre. Never the property.
svg.desc: The Stagehand Homage Rule. Borrow the grammar: light, palette mood, type feel, camera language, edit rhythm and sound texture. Never ship franchise names or logos, characters, named places or terms, quotes, scores, stills, or the franchise typefaces. Below: the naming rule (codename only), the swap test, and the commentary exception.
svg.text: REF STC V1.0 / REEL V6 · FIG STC-09
Evoke the genre. Never the property.
Themes borrow a genre's grammar and nothing a studio owns. A style can't be owned; logos, characters and specific expression can.
Open-license faces with the right temperament.
Push-ins, crawls, tracking shots, crash zooms.
On the beat, on twos, held pauses.
Hum, hiss, tape, room tone. Never a melody.
NEVER SHIP, AT ANY THEME OR INTENSITY
Franchise names, logos, wordmarks or title lockups, including look-alikes.
Characters, creatures, likenesses, costumes or telling silhouettes.
Named places, organizations, ships, products or invented terms.
Scores, sound-alikes of a theme melody, signature sound effects.
Stills, frames, posters or traced compositions of specific shots.
The franchise's own typefaces. Use the open fonts on each card.
Public pages, meta tags, alt text and client work use the
codename only. Internal briefs may name the inspiration.
Picture the theme swapped for its nearest genre neighbor.
Anything that only makes sense as one property gets cut or
A story about a film may name it as factual reference, with no
logos or studio assets. A licensed look escalates to Barry.
BHIL · STAGEHAND THEME CODEX · FIG STC-09
